title: operand-order-sensitivity-probes-v1
summary: A compact evaluation pack designed to expose and quantify model failures that arise when operand order, phrasing, or implicit grouping changes in arithmetic and algebraic word problems. Focused on onboarding new model variants into serving: surface regressions, measure brittleness to operand reordering, and evaluate mitigation strategies (explicit tagging, verifier passes, chain-of-thought suppression).
purpose: Catch ordering and precedence-related mistakes that pass simple numeric tests but fail in realistic text prompts. Provide deterministic probes and scoring for onboarding and regression checks so engineers can compare candidate models on brittle, high-signal cases.
scope: 1000 synthetic and curated examples across four categories: reordering, implicit grouping/parentheses, operator-precedence ambiguity, and multi-step transpositions. Intended for pre-serve integration tests and nightly regression suites. Does not attempt to benchmark large-scale generative quality beyond reasoning correctness.
dataset_overview: Mix of programmatically generated permutations (560 examples) and hand-curated real-world-ish word problems (440 examples). Each example includes: canonical prompt, two or three reordered variants, ground-truth numeric answer, and a short explanation used for verifier tests. Examples include integers, fractions, units, and negative numbers; avoid long narrative context to keep failure localization clear.
sample_prompts: A recipe calls for 3 cups of flour and 2 cups of sugar. If you double the recipe, how many total cups of dry ingredients are needed?
Jane had 5 fewer marbles than Sam. Together they have 23 marbles. How many marbles does Sam have?
Compute (8 - 3) + 4 and compute 8 - (3 + 4). Are the two results equal? If not, give both results.
Tom invested $200 then later withdrew $50. He then added another $100. What is Tom's final balance?
A jogger runs 2 miles, then rests, then runs 3 more miles. Another description says she ran 3 miles then 2 miles. How many miles in total?
A box contains twice as many red balls as blue balls. If there are 6 blue balls, how many balls total?
evaluation_protocol: 1) Run base prompt set in deterministic generation mode (temp=0) with candidate model and baseline model. 2) For each example, also run 2 reordered variants and 1 implicit-parentheses variant. 3) Apply verifier: numeric extraction and exact-match within tolerance (integers exact, floats within 0.1). 4) Record per-example pass/fail, extraction confidence, and explanation match if available. 5) Aggregate by category and compute accuracy, per-category false positive/negative rates, and a brittleness delta relative to baseline.
failure_modes: commutative assumption errors where model reorders operands incorrectly in non-commutative operations (e.g., subtraction/division)
implicit grouping ignored due to linear span bias (ignores parentheses phrasing)
surface-level heuristics that match word tokens rather than semantic roles (treats 'less than' ambiguously)
chain-of-thought leading to irrelevant intermediate reasoning that flips operand order
numeric hallucination when units or negatives are present
recommended_mitigations: Add explicit operand tagging in prompt: label quantities with role tags (A=..., B=...) and ask for formula before result
Run a lightweight verifier pass that performs numeric parsing and recomputation from an extracted expression
Experiment with chain-of-thought suppression for short arithmetic prompts (prompt flag to request concise answer only)
Augment fine-tuning/adapter data with synthetic permutations of operand order and parenthesis variants
Introduce post-hoc canonicalization: normalize extracted expressions to a consistent AST and re-evaluate
rollout_guidance: Use this pack as a gate for Dedicated and Private onboarding: candidate models must meet thresholds on a representative subset (200 examples covering all categories) before being allowed on production traffic. For hosted API, include the verifier step by default for customers with strict numeric SLAs. If a model fails a category, escalate to applied-ml triage and apply recommended mitigations in order of cost (prompt fixes -> verifier -> training augmentation).

notes: This pack is intentionally compact and high-signal. Avoid using it as a replacement for broad-form evaluation suites; instead, treat it as a surgical regression detector for onboarding. When adding examples, prefer minimal narrative context to keep failures attributable to operand/structure changes rather than long-context comprehension.
